briefings.tldr: Stripe is repositioning itself as the "economic infrastructure for the AI era," responding to a 2026 inflection point where autonomous agents have become primary economic actors.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Stripe is repositioning itself as the "economic infrastructure for the AI era," responding to a 2026 inflection point where autonomous agents have become primary economic actors. Key innovations include real-time "token" billing, a dedicated payments blockchain (Tempo), and the ability for agents to autonomously deploy code and execute financial transactions.

## The "Agentic" Economy & Autonomous Commerce
Stripe reports a "parabolic rise" in new business creation in 2026, driven by a shift from human-led commerce to agent-led transactions.
*   **Agentic Commerce Suite:** A new suite allowing businesses to make products "legible" to AI agents. Partnerships with Google (Gemini), Meta, and OpenAI enable customers to buy products directly within AI interfaces.
*   **Stripe Projects:** A tool for "vibe deployment" that allows AI agents (like Claude Code) to autonomously provision databases, sandboxes, and hosting to launch apps in seconds.
*   **Link Wallet for Agents:** A secure credentialing system that allows users to set spending "policies" for their AI agents, allowing them to buy and sell software autonomously without exposing raw card data.
*   **Machine Payments Protocol (MPP):** An open standard for service-to-service payments, enabling APIs to signal to agents that payment is required and how to facilitate it over HTTP.

## Financial Infrastructure for the AI Era
To handle the speed of AI agents, Stripe has re-architected its stack to support high-velocity, micro-scale transactions.
*   **Metronome & Real-Time Metering:** Following the acquisition of Metronome, Stripe now supports real-time token counting and "rating," allowing AI companies to bill for compute/tokens as they are consumed.
*   **Tempo Blockchain:** Developed with Paradigm, Tempo is a payments-optimized blockchain designed for "streaming payments." It enables sub-cent micropayments via stablecoins to prevent credit risk in high-speed AI environments.
*   **Stablecoin Integration:** Stablecoins are now a first-class citizen in the Stripe ecosystem, used for global payouts to 160 countries and real-time settlement for AI agents.

## The Stripe "Financial Operating System"
Stripe is moving beyond simple payment processing to become a comprehensive, programmable treasury and data hub.
*   **Stripe Treasury:** A new financial OS offering multi-currency accounts (USD, EUR, GBP, and stablecoins) with 2% cashback on card spend and FDIC insurance in the US.
*   **Instant Transfers:** Businesses on the Stripe network can now send money to one another instantly and for free, bypassing traditional banking delays.
*   **Stripe Database:** A Postgres database that provides real-time, structured access to all Stripe data, designed to be queried by both humans and AI agents.
*   **Custom Objects & Workflows:** A "made-to-order" version of Stripe where businesses can define their own logic (e.g., insurance claims or shipping numbers) natively within the Stripe dashboard.

## Next-Generation Fraud & Intelligence
As fraud evolves into "token theft" and trial abuse, Stripe is leveraging its network data to provide "Signals" to developers.
*   **Radar Upgrades:** New protections specifically targeting AI-native fraud, such as "Multi-Account Abuse" (stealing user credits) and "Free Trial Abuse" (burning inference costs on non-converting users).
*   **Stripe Signals:** A new API providing direct access to Stripe’s network intelligence. It returns scores and explanations for transaction risk, business trustworthiness, and customer conversion probability.
*   **Smart Disputes:** An AI-driven tool that compiles evidence for chargebacks, reportedly recovering 18% more revenue and winning cases 3x more often.

## Notable Quotes

> "The basic idea in Stripe is that money is data... Standing here in 2026, it’s obviously become quite essential. Stripe is building the economic infrastructure for the AI era."
— **Patrick Collison**, CEO of Stripe

> "Payments will pivot from being a moment to being a policy... where you set guardrails for your agent to spend on your behalf."
— **Ginger Baker**, VP of Product, Meta

> "Any business on Stripe can now send money to any other business on Stripe, instantly and for free. Instant and free: two words you don’t usually hear together in finance."
— **Neetika**, Stripe (Money Management)

> "In the era of agentic coding, building an app shouldn’t feel like assembling IKEA furniture... Projects programmatically provisions services, manages usage, and navigates billing directly from the command line."
— **Will Gaybrick**, President of Technology and Business, Stripe

briefings.tldr: Stripe is positioning itself as the primary "economic infrastructure" for the AI era, transitioning from human-centric transactions to a world where AI agents act as independent economic actors through usage-based billing, stablecoin micropayments, and deeper platform integrations.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Stripe is positioning itself as the primary "economic infrastructure" for the AI era, transitioning from human-centric transactions to a world where AI agents act as independent economic actors through usage-based billing, stablecoin micropayments, and deeper platform integrations.

## The Rise of Agentic Commerce
*   **AI as an Economic Actor:** Collison argues that the economy is shifting from human-to-human transactions to "agentic" commerce, where AI agents make purchasing decisions.
    *   **Delegated Decisions:** Consumers are moving from using AI for research to allowing agents to execute small tasks, such as purchasing domain names or grocery ingredients.
    *   **B2B Shift:** Tech companies (e.g., Cloudflare, Vercel) are increasingly selling services directly to "coding agents" rather than human procurement officers.
*   **Google Partnership:** Stripe is integrating with Google’s Gemini and AI-powered search to allow users to complete purchases directly within the AI interface rather than being redirected to external websites.
*   **Product Discovery:** Major brands like Best Buy and Kate Spade are adopting these tools to stay ahead of how AI is changing consumer discovery and checkout habits.

## New Economic Models: Tokens and Micropayments
*   **Usage-Based Billing:** AI has broken the traditional "per-seat" subscription model due to high inference costs. 
    *   **Metered Billing:** Companies like OpenAI and Anthropic now require "per-token" or "per-request" billing infrastructure.
    *   **Metronome Acquisition:** Stripe is leveraging its acquisition of Metronome to help AI companies manage these complex, high-volume metering challenges.
*   **Stablecoins and "Tempo":** While micropayments have historically failed with humans due to "decision friction," they are ideal for AI agents.
    *   **Streaming Payments:** Stripe has incubated a blockchain called **Tempo** specifically designed for payment use cases.
    *   **Crypto Utility:** Collison views stablecoins as the most viable medium for real-time, autonomous agent transactions.

## Security and the "AI Singularity"
*   **The Singularity Timeline:** Collison semi-seriously dates the "Singularity" to January 1, 2024, noting that AI is now in a state of "recursive self-improvement" where coding models are significantly accelerating the development of the next generation of AI.
*   **Evolving Fraud Vectors:** AI companies face unique "shrinkage" issues, such as bad actors attempting to steal inference or abuse free trials.
    *   **Stripe Radar:** In a single month, Stripe’s security tools blocked over 3 million attempted thefts targeting top-tier AI clients.
    *   **Network Effect:** Stripe uses its "bird's-eye view" of global internet transactions to identify and block novel AI-specific fraud patterns.

## Stripe’s Corporate Strategy and Identity
*   **Infrastructure vs. Consumer Brand:** Despite having 250 million users on its "Link" checkout service, Stripe remains focused on being the invisible "plumbing" of the internet rather than a consumer-facing app.
*   **M&A Stance:** Collison declined to comment on reports regarding a potential acquisition of PayPal assets, maintaining Stripe's policy of not commenting on market speculation.
*   **Growth Objective:** The core mission remains "growing the GDP of the internet" by lowering friction, regardless of whether the buyer is a human or a machine.

> "It’s never been the case in technology when you get a way more convenient way of working for consumers that they pick the less convenient one. It’s never happened." — **John Collison**

> "The coding models have gotten so good that they are now contributing in a significant way to the rate of improvement of AI itself... recursive self-improvement is the industry term here." — **John Collison**

> "For any kind of an agentic product, micropayments via stablecoins makes total sense... we think as you think about streaming payments, it actually could be a really interesting application for crypto." — **John Collison**

briefings.title: The AI Frontier and How to Spot Billion-Dollar Companies Before Everyone Else — Elad Gil
briefings.tldr: The AI landscape is currently defined by a "personal IPO" for top talent and a temporary compute ceiling caused by memory bottlenecks, creating a unique two-year window of market parity and a critical 12-18 month exit opportunity for non-durable startups.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The AI landscape is currently defined by a "personal IPO" for top talent and a temporary compute ceiling caused by memory bottlenecks, creating a unique two-year window of market parity and a critical 12-18 month exit opportunity for non-durable startups.

## The Talent "Personal IPO" and Compute Bottlenecks
* **The Personal IPO:** Elad Gil describes a shift where a small class of AI researchers (50–500 people) effectively experienced a personal IPO.
    * Driven by Meta’s aggressive bidding, pay packages have surged to between tens and hundreds of millions of dollars.
    * This wealth allows top researchers to pivot to "big science" or passion projects rather than staying tethered to a single corporate mission.
* **Compute Constraints:** All major labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI) are currently hitting a "ceiling" on model scaling.
    * **Memory Bottleneck:** While chip packaging was the previous constraint, the current bottleneck is High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), largely controlled by Korean manufacturers.
    * **Supply Chain Parity:** Because no single lab can secure 10x the compute of its rivals due to these supply chain limits, the major players will likely remain at roughly the same capability level for the next two years.
* **The Revenue Sprint:** AI companies are reaching scale at unprecedented speeds. 
    * OpenAI and Anthropic reached $1 billion in revenue in roughly one year, whereas Google took four. 
    * These companies are approaching a run rate representing ~0.1% to 1% of US GDP.

## Strategic Timing for Founders and Exits
* **The 12-18 Month Exit Window:** Gil advises founders of successful AI companies to look hard at exiting within the next 12–18 months.
    * **Historical Precedent:** In every cycle (Auto, Dot-com, SaaS), 90-95% of companies eventually go bust. 
    * **Value Maximization:** Many current AI startups may face commoditization or competition from the labs themselves. Selling during this high-valuation window might be the value-maximizing move before the "second derivative of growth" plateaus.
* **Durable Advantage Criteria:** Gil identifies what makes a company worth keeping long-term:
    * **Workflow Integration:** Durability comes from "change management"—embedding the tool so deeply into a company’s workflow that it is hard to extract.
    * **Unit of Labor:** Generative AI is shifting from selling "seats" (SaaS) to selling "units of labor/cognition," which opens previously closed markets like legal (e.g., Harvey) and health (e.g., Abridge).

## The Investor’s Lens: Market over Team
* **Market-First Philosophy:** Gil prioritizes market over team (90% of the time). He notes that "amazing teams are crushed by terrible markets, but reasonably crappy teams can do well in great ones."
* **The Power Law:** Investment returns are highly concentrated. Gil cites research suggesting that only ~10 companies drive 80% of all technology returns over a 20-year period.
* **Spotting "Open" Markets:** AI is currently "consensus" rather than "contrarian." Gil argues that being consensus is currently the smartest move because the technology has "plugged into" all white-collar work and language-based data simultaneously.
* **Aggressive Distribution:** Gil debunks the "build it and they will come" myth. 
    * Google spent hundreds of millions on browser toolbar distribution.
    * Facebook used aggressive ad strategies in Europe to "buy" network liquidity.
    * Successful companies pair a great product engine with a relentless distribution engine (sales/marketing).

## Using AI for Research and Due Diligence
* **AI as a Research Partner:** Gil uses multiple models (OpenAI, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini) simultaneously for deep-dive research.
    * **Cross-Model Verification:** He prompts models to aggregate clinical trial data, provide primary sources, and double-check outputs against one another.
    * **"Cold Reading":** He experiments with uploading photos of founders to AI to assess personality micro-features (e.g., genuine smiles vs. furrowed brows) to predict behavior and humor, finding surprising signal.
* **Truth-Seeking in Medicine:** Gil uses AI to investigate diagnostic shifts, such as the 3,000% increase in autism diagnoses. He found that the primary driver is often diagnostic criteria and school incentives rather than paternal/maternal age.

## Notable Quotes
> **Elad Gil:** "There are moments in time where it’s very smart to be contrarian. And there are moments in time where being consensus is the smartest possible thing you can do. And I think right now we’re in a moment in time where being consensus is very right."

> **Elad Gil:** "If your co-founder is kind of like your spouse... your board members are like your in-laws. You have to see them at Thanksgiving... and if they’re an investor, you can’t fire them."

> **Tim Ferriss:** "It just struck me that... if you want money, ask for advice, and if you want advice, ask for money. It goes the other way around, too: if you offer a bunch of advice, oftentimes you get to give money [invest]."

> **Elad Gil:** "We’re going from selling software and SaaS and we’re moving into a world where we’re selling human labor equivalents. We’re selling work hours or labor hours of cognition."

briefings.title: Think You Know AI? 25 Startups Prove You Wrong
briefings.tldr: AI is evolving beyond digital chatbots into "physical world" applications, leveraging edge computing and NVIDIA’s stack to solve global challenges in agriculture, climate resilience, energy security, and personalized medicine.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** AI is evolving beyond digital chatbots into "physical world" applications, leveraging edge computing and NVIDIA’s stack to solve global challenges in agriculture, climate resilience, energy security, and personalized medicine.

## Agriculture and Environmental Sustainability
AI is being deployed to optimize food production for a growing population of 8 billion while reducing chemical dependency and waste.

*   **Autonomous Pollination Management:** Startups like **BeeWise** use "luxury apartments" for bees—automated hives equipped with computer vision and edge computing to monitor colony health, detect parasites, and manage pollinators without manual human inspection.
*   **Chemical-Free Weeding:** 
    *   **Mechanical Intervention:** Solar and wind-powered robots use vision at the edge to identify weeds and physically pull them from the ground.
    *   **Laser Technology:** Companies like **Carbon Robotics** utilize micro-focused lasers to "kill weeds with energy" rather than herbicides, allowing for precision farming at scale.
*   **Waste Stream Optimization:** AI-powered scanning systems analyze municipal waste flows to provide data on recycling potential, followed by robotic sorting arms that extract recyclables from waste streams more efficiently than manual labor.
*   **Data Visibility:** AI is filling the "data gap" for the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals; currently, 68% of environmental goals lack sufficient data to track progress.

## Community Protection and Climate Resilience
The focus in disaster management has shifted to "shortening the gap" between a threat occurring and detection through advanced sensing.

*   **Wildfire Detection:**
    *   **On-Orbit Processing:** Startups are putting GPUs on satellites to process high-fidelity images in space, beaming down only the detections rather than massive raw data files.
    *   **Ground-Based Sensors:** Persistent, horizontal-view sensors in forests use edge models to detect micro-signals of smoke or fire before they escalate.
*   **Next-Gen Weather Forecasting:** **ClimaVision** is deploying private radar networks to augment legacy weather sensors, providing high-fidelity data in "gap" areas to better predict extreme weather events in dense urban centers.
*   **Urban Flow Analytics:** Moving beyond simple traffic cameras to 3D understanding of city systems, allowing municipalities to track the flow of people and goods as integrated systems rather than isolated data points.

## Energy Security and Infrastructure
The 21st-century power grid is transitioning from a one-way utility model to a complex, bidirectional "prosumer" network requiring AI for stability.

*   **Vegetation Management:** AI analyzes satellite imagery to identify foliage encroaching on power lines, allowing utilities to move from reactive repairs to proactive, "persistent defense" strategies.
*   **Digital Twins for Utilities:** Physically driven, sensor-informed digital models allow grid operators to simulate stress tests and predict failures before they happen, ensuring more equitable power restoration during storms.
*   **Grid Complexity Management:** As EVs and solar rooftops turn consumers into producers, AI manages the "squared complexity" of multi-directional energy flows that legacy models cannot handle.

## Individual Safety and Next-Gen Science
AI is being used to provide personalized support in private moments and to accelerate complex scientific discovery.

*   **Assistive Technology:** Headsets with onboard sensors allow the visually impaired to "see without sight," using car-like spatial awareness to navigate environments and interact with objects independently.
*   **Emergency Response:** AI analyzes voice patterns and stress signals during 911 calls to assist dispatchers with early diagnosis and triage, reducing cognitive load during high-stress moments.
*   **Medical Research Advancements:**
    *   **Federated Learning:** This "privacy-first" approach moves the AI model to the hospital’s data enclave rather than moving patient data to the cloud, allowing models to train on sensitive records without compromising privacy.
    *   **In-Silico Testing:** Researchers use digital twins of biology (such as "digital tumors") to test-drive drug treatments and personalized therapies before they are administered to a patient.

> "The trend of the 20th century was just this massive expansion of the world... in the 21st century, as we see AI start to bring us together, we've seen its ability to interact with a huge array of problems... things that we didn't think were possible without it." — **Chris, NVIDIA**

> "If we cannot see these problems, we cannot measure them... we're just flying blind. The opportunity here is: how can we use AI to get more visibility into these systems?" — **Joshi, NVIDIA**

> "AI is enabling the analysis of extensive data sets, uncovering hidden patterns, and accelerating the pace of discovery... we can augment our amazing scientists and researchers with the complete information." — **Joshi, NVIDIA**

briefings.title: WATCH LIVE: BOE Governor Andrew Bailey to speak after rate decision
briefings.tldr: The Bank of England held its benchmark interest rate steady at 3.75% in an 8-1 vote, taking previous expectations of rate cuts off the table due to Middle East conflict-driven energy price volatility.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
The Bank of England held its benchmark interest rate steady at 3.75% in an 8-1 vote, taking previous expectations of rate cuts off the table due to Middle East conflict-driven energy price volatility. To navigate this uncertainty, the bank introduced three distinct economic scenarios ranging from a rapid return to its 2% inflation target to a severe 6% inflation spike that would require aggressive interest rate hikes.

---

## The Rate Decision and the "Active Hold"

* **The 8-1 Rate Vote:** The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted to maintain the bank rate at 3.75%. 
    * **The Dissenting Voice:** Chief Economist Huw Pill was the sole hawk, voting instead for a 25 basis point hike to 4.0%.
    * **Market Relief:** Victoria Clarke (Chief UK Economist at Santander) noted that the 8-1 split came as a sigh of relief for markets that feared a more aggressive hawkish shift.
* **An "Active Hold" Stance:** Governor Andrew Bailey emphasized that holding the rate is an active, deliberate policy decision rather than a passive "wait-and-see" approach. 
* **Rate Cuts Off the Table:** The MPC officially abandoned its previous projections for interest rate cuts this year. Bailey confirmed that the "headroom" previously reserved for cuts will instead be used to absorb the inflationary impact of the geopolitical shock.

## Three Economic Scenarios for the UK

Because of the extreme volatility of global oil and gas prices, the Bank of England departed from its traditional single forecast to present three illustrative scenarios:

* **Scenario A (Benign Case):** Assumes energy prices follow market futures curves downward and consumer demand drops sharply due to weak sentiment.
    * **Inflation Outcome:** No second-round wage-price effects occur, and inflation falls below the 2% target by the end of next year without further rate hikes.
* **Scenario B (Moderate/Base Case):** Assumes more persistent energy price pressures due to slow repairs of damaged gas infrastructure in the Gulf.
    * **Inflation Outcome:** Modest second-round effects are felt, but inflation gradually returns to the 2% target within two to three years. Reversing out the previously assumed 55 basis point market rate cuts is expected to accommodate this scenario.
* **Scenario C (Severe Shock Case):** Assumes prolonged disruptions pushing oil to $130 a barrel and gas to 210 pence per therm, alongside strong wage-price feedback loops.
    * **Inflation Outcome:** Inflation peaks above 6% in early 2027 and remains above the 2% target after three years.
    * **Policy Response:** This scenario would require a materially tighter monetary policy, potentially pushing interest rates to 5.25% or higher, and would likely trigger a mild recession.

## Labor Market and Wage Dynamics

* **Labor Market Slack:** The MPC noted that the UK labor market has significantly more slack now than during the 2022 energy crisis. This weakness is expected to lower employee bargaining power and prevent aggressive wage-price spirals.
    * **Unemployment Outlook:** The unemployment rate recently dipped toward 5% but is projected to rise back to 6% under a severe shock scenario.
* **Private vs. Public Sector Pay:** 
    * Private sector wage growth is moderating toward levels comfortable for the bank.
    * Public sector pay remains elevated and represents a key domestic metric to watch.
* **Indirect Energy Impacts on Food:** High energy costs are expected to feed indirectly into food production and distribution. While short-term forecasts project food inflation at 4.6% through September, reports from Bank of England agents suggest it could climb to a range of 6% to 7% by the end of the year.

## Market Conditions and Quantitative Tightening

* **Tighter Financial Conditions:** Financial markets have already responded to the geopolitical crisis, pushing 10-year gilt yields comfortably above 5%.
* **Commodity Volatility:** Bailey highlighted the extreme volatility facing policymakers, pointing out that the Brent crude oil price fluctuated by over $10 a barrel in a single morning.
* **Quantitative Tightening (QT) Here to Stay:** Victoria Clarke observed that the Bank of England is highly unlikely to pause its QT program unless the UK experiences an extremely severe episode of gilt market stress, and even then, any pause would only be temporary.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "The prospect of cuts which we were after all talking about at this press conference three months ago is not on the table now."  
> — **Andrew Bailey**, Governor of the Bank of England

> "We have really drawn attention... to the continued looseness of the labor market. And that is a very different position for the labor market than we were in in 2022."  
> — **Dave Ramsden**, Deputy Governor for Markets and Banking

> "The MPC's decision to hold bank rate today is based on two key judgments. First, that continued weakness in activity and the labor market is likely to lessen the strength of second-round effects... Second, that uncertainty about the strength of second-round effects means that monetary policy needs to balance the costs of leaning too little against these effects against the costs of responding too much."  
> — **Andrew Bailey**, Governor of the Bank of England

briefings.title: WATCH LIVE: European Central Bank Press Conference with President Christine Lagarde
briefings.tldr: The ECB Governing Council kept its three key interest rates unchanged, adopting a strict data-dependent, meeting-by-meeting approach to return medium-term inflation to its 2% target amidst intensified geopolitical risks, rising energy prices, and slower economic growth.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
The ECB Governing Council kept its three key interest rates unchanged, adopting a strict data-dependent, meeting-by-meeting approach to return medium-term inflation to its 2% target amidst intensified geopolitical risks, rising energy prices, and slower economic growth.

***

## Monetary Policy Stance and the June Decision Framework

* **Interest Rate Decision:** The Governing Council unanimously decided to keep the three key ECB interest rates unchanged. 
    * **Policy Rationale:** President Christine Lagarde characterized the choice as "an informed decision on the basis of yet insufficient information," noting that while hard data aligns with March projections, extreme geopolitical uncertainty requires the Council to wait for June's updated projections and scenario analyses.
    * **Rate Path Flexibility:** The ECB is not pre-committing to any specific rate path. Future decisions will remain strictly data-dependent, determined on a meeting-by-meeting basis.
* **Reaction Function:** The ECB's policy reaction remains anchored on three core pillars:
    * Maintaining a symmetric 2% medium-term inflation target.
    * Calibrating the forcefulness of policy response based on the size and sustainability of any target deviations.
    * Assessing incoming economic data, underlying inflation dynamics, and the strength of monetary policy transmission.
* **The June Outlook:** The next policy meeting in six weeks will leverage fresh data on wage settlements, collective agreements, corporate profit margins, and commodity price trends to reassess whether further tightening or adjustments are necessary.

## Macroeconomic Outlook and Risk Profiles

* **Growth Performance and Projections:** The euro area's economic growth is slowing but avoids stagnation. 
    * **Real GDP:** Grew by 0.1% in Q1 2026 (preliminary flash estimate), driven primarily by domestic demand and a resilient labor market.
    * **Growth Outlook:** The ECB projects GDP growth of 0.8% for 2026, rising to 1.2% and 1.3% in subsequent years. 
    * **Stagflation Dismissed:** Lagarde explicitly rejected "stagflation" as an accurate label for the current environment, pointing to low unemployment (6.2% in March) and positive growth forecasts, which contrast sharply with the persistent stagnation and high unemployment of the 1970s.
* **Geopolitical Downside Risks:** The ongoing war in the Middle East represents a major drag on economic sentiment, supply chain logistics, and trade. Prolonged closure of key shipping routes could force production cuts due to critical input shortages.
* **Inflation Dynamics and Upside Risks:** Inflation rose to 3% in April (up from 2.6% in March and 1.9% in February), driven heavily by energy costs.
    * **Energy Price Spike:** Energy price inflation jumped to 10.9% in April, compared to 5.1% in March, following Middle East disruptions.
    * **Core Inflation:** Inflation excluding food and energy decreased slightly to 2.2% (down from 2.3% in March), supported by a decline in services inflation to 3.0%.
    * **Second-Round Effects:** The ECB is closely monitoring whether high energy costs spill over into broader wage-setting and long-term inflation expectations, though current surveys show no signs of major second-round wage-price spirals.

## Financial Sector Dynamics and Credit Conditions

* **Liquidity and Operational Framework:** Eurosystem central bank reserves have decreased from their peak to just under €2.6 trillion. 
    * **Abundance of Liquidity:** Despite the decline, Lagarde emphasized that the banking system still possesses significant excess liquidity, and no new liquidity tools are currently under discussion.
    * **Framework Review:** The Eurosystem is actively preparing a timetable and methodology to calibrate its operational framework, ensuring it remains fit for purpose and supportive of financial stability.
* **Tightening Financial Conditions:** Market-based financing costs have risen since the outbreak of Middle East hostilities.
    * **Debt and Lending Rates:** The cost of market-based debt issuance rose to 3.9% in March (up from 3.5% in February). Prior to the conflict, bank lending rates to firms and mortgage rates stood at 3.5% and 3.4% respectively.
    * **Credit Supply and Demand:** The Q1 Bank Lending Survey indicates that credit standards for corporate loans have tightened due to banks' heightened risk perceptions. Concurrently, corporate demand for loans—particularly for fixed investment—declined.
* **European Banking Integration:** Vice-President Luis de Guindos reiterated the ECB’s support for a single banking jurisdiction within Europe, advocating for the free flow of capital and liquidity across member states to bolster systemic resilience.

## Fiscal Policy and Structural Recommendations

* **The "3 Ts" of Fiscal Support:** The ECB urges euro area governments to ensure all fiscal measures implemented in response to energy price shocks remain:
    * **Temporary:** Avoiding permanent deficits.
    * **Targeted:** Directed exclusively at vulnerable populations.
    * **Tailored:** Designed to maintain price signals that encourage energy conservation.
    * **GDP Impact:** Currently committed fiscal support measures across the euro area represent roughly 0.1% of GDP.
* **Structural Reforms:** To reduce dependence on fossil fuels and bolster productivity, the Governing Council stressed the importance of accelerating the energy transition, completing the European savings and investment union, and simplifying single market regulations.
* **Strategic Autonomy:** Swift adoption of the digital euro regulation is highlighted as vital for Europe's payment system competitiveness, strategic autonomy, and financial integration.

***

## Notable Quotes

> "If I was to summarize for you what we decided today, I would say that we made an informed decision on the basis of yet insufficient information."  
> — **Christine Lagarde, ECB President**

> "We project growth of 0.8% followed by 1.2% followed by 1.3%. I wouldn't call that stagnation, sorry. It's lower growth, granted, in '26, but we're not in stagnation, let alone recession."  
> — **Christine Lagarde, ECB President**

> "We are in favor of a single jurisdiction for the European banks with free flow of capital and liquidity."  
> — **Luis de Guindos, ECB Vice-President**

briefings.title: WATCH LIVE: Senate Banking Committee votes on Kevin Warsh's nomination for Federal Reserve chair
briefings.tldr: The Senate Banking Committee voted 13-11 to advance Kevin Warsh’s nomination for Federal Reserve Chair to the full Senate, following a contentious debate regarding central bank independence and allegations of executive interference by the Trump administration.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The Senate Banking Committee voted 13-11 to advance Kevin Warsh’s nomination for Federal Reserve Chair to the full Senate, following a contentious debate regarding central bank independence and allegations of executive interference by the Trump administration.

## Committee Vote and Procedural Context
* **The Vote:** The committee moved in-block to report Kevin Warsh favorably for a seat on the Board of Governors (term expiring 2040) and a four-year term as Chairman.
    * The final tally was 13 in favor and 11 opposed, reflecting a strict party-line split.
* **The Trigger for the Markup:** Senator Elizabeth Warren (Ranking Member) noted that the vote only proceeded after US Attorney Jenny Durkan announced the closure of a criminal investigation into current Fed Chair Jerome Powell, a move Warren characterized as a political "trigger" to allow the nomination to move forward.
* **DOJ Assurances:** Senator Thom Tillis defended the timing, stating he received personal assurances from the Department of Justice that the investigation into the Fed was being handled appropriately by the Inspector General, effectively resolving his previous concerns about the probe.

## Allegations of Executive Overreach
* **Independence Concerns:** Democrats, led by Senators Warren and Raphael Warnock, argued that advancing Warsh facilitates an "illegal attempt to seize control" of the Federal Reserve.
    * **Threats to Personnel:** Critics highlighted President Trump’s repeated threats to fire Chair Powell and his ongoing legal attempts to remove Governor Lisa Cook.
    * **Ongoing Investigations:** Senator Warren entered statements into the record from the President and DOJ officials suggesting that criminal investigations into current Fed leadership are "not dropped" but merely paused or shifted to different agencies.
* **The "Sock Puppet" Critique:** Senator Warren labeled Warsh a "Trump sock puppet," citing his refusal during hearings to acknowledge that Donald Trump lost the 2020 election as evidence that he lacks the independence required for the role.

## Candidate Fitness and Financial Transparency
* **Financial Disclosures:** Senator Warren raised concerns over Warsh’s personal finances, noting he holds more than $100 million in "secret financial assets."
    * **Divestment Plan:** Critics argued Warsh has failed to disclose if his plan to divest involves significant financial backing from billionaire investors.
* **Past Performance:** Opponents pointed to Warsh's tenure as a Fed Governor during the 2008 financial crisis, describing his record as "catastrophic" for American families while favoring Wall Street.
* **Refusal to Answer "Hypotheticals":** Senator Warnock expressed deep dissatisfaction with Warsh’s written responses to questions. 
    * **Firing Scenario:** When asked if he would leave the Fed if the President attempted to unlawfully fire him, Warsh responded that he would "not answer hypothetical questions," a stance Warnock called "woefully insufficient" given the President's actual attempts to fire sitting governors.

## Economic Outlook and "Bidenomics"
* **Republican Perspective:** Republican members argued that Warsh is "battle-tested" and uniquely qualified to lead the country out of the "bind of Bidenomics."
    * **Inflation Control:** Proponents blamed the previous administration for 9% inflation and argued that Warsh would provide a more consistent, less political focus on the needs of American households.
* **Democratic Perspective:** Senator Warnock countered that the current "Trump economy" is failing working families, particularly in Georgia, and that the Fed must remain independent to protect jobs and affordability rather than serve the President’s "poll numbers."

## Notable Quotes
> "A vote today by this committee to advance Mr. Warsh will bring the President one step closer to completing his illegal attempt to seize control of the Fed and to artificially juice the economy." 
— **Senator Elizabeth Warren**, Ranking Member

> "Kevin Warsh's leadership is absolutely essential now at the Federal Reserve than ever before. Frankly, his time as a former governor of the Federal Reserve during the crisis makes him battle-tested and ready to serve and not only serve, but to lead."
— **Senate Banking Committee Republican** (In support of the nomination)

> "I asked, 'If President Trump or any future president attempts to unlawfully fire you without cause, would you leave?'... His response: 'I will not answer hypothetical questions of this nature.' Well, this isn't a hypothetical question." 
— **Senator Raphael Warnock**

> "I’ve got confidence that this investigation is over... [Senator Warren] is flatly wrong on every point she just tried to make." 
— **Senator Thom Tillis**
